extracted.intended_audience: product marketers, startup founders, and PR/communications professionals preparing product launch press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for writing and distributing product-launch press releases that are newsworthy, demoable, and customer-validated for tech/product companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: New capability that wasn't possible before
rubrics_metrics.description: New capability that wasn't possible before
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The launch should enable a genuinely new functionality or outcome (not merely iterative or cosmetic). This is listed as a primary requirement under 'What Makes a Releasable Product Launch' and reiterated in the Quality Rubric as 'Genuinely new capability.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant improvement over prior version
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant improvement over prior version
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the product is an update, the change must be a material step forward versus the prior version to justify a press release (not just incremental performance tweaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tied to industry trend or market shift
rubrics_metrics.description: Tied to industry trend or market shift
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position the launch in the context of a broader trend or market change to increase newsworthiness and relevance to press and analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer-validated through beta
rubrics_metrics.description: Customer-validated through beta
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of customer validation (beta testers, named customers, measurable outcomes) is required to make the launch credible and quotable; appears both in 'What Makes a Releasable Product Launch' and in the Body Paragraph structure (Customer Validation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demoable to journalists immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Demoable to journalists immediately
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The product should be demonstrable (screenshots, short demo video, live demo) so press can verify claims quickly. This reduces friction for coverage and is called out as a release requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not issue a release for minor feature updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor feature updates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor, incremental features do not warrant a press release; treat these as product update notes or release notes instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not issue a release for UI redesigns without functional change
rubrics_metrics.description: UI redesigns without functional change
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual-only changes that don't change capability are not newsworthy; avoid framing them as product launches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not issue a release for bug fixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Bug fixes (no matter how big)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even substantial bug fixes are not considered launch-worthy; reserve press releases for new capabilities or major improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not issue a release for internal-only improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal-only improvements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Back-end or internal optimizations that customers don't experience directly should not be launched via press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'we added support for X' unless X is significant
rubrics_metrics.description: "We added support for X" (unless X is significant)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding support for a platform/format/third-party integration should only be a release if the supported item is strategically important or opens a materially new capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline format
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Company] Launches [Product] to [New Capability]"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear, benefit-oriented headline that follows the template. Examples provided: 'Acme Launches Workflow Builder for No-Code Automation' and 'BetaCorp Releases AI Code Reviewer Cutting PR Review Time 60%'. Keep it specific and outcome-focused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede template
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Company] today launched [Product], [brief description] that enables [users] to [new capability]. The product is available [today/beta/waitlist] for [price/free]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with the announcement, succinct product description, who it helps, the new capability enabled, and immediate availability/pricing status. Keep the lede concise and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 1: The Problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 1: The Problem — What pain point this solves; Who experiences this pain; Why existing solutions fall short
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start by describing the real customer problem and the limitations of current alternatives. Be specific about the users affected and the severity/frequency of the pain to justify the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 2: The Solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 2: The Solution — How the product works (specific mechanism); Key features that enable the capability; What makes it different
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the mechanism and features that enable the claimed capability, and highlight differentiators versus competitors or previous approaches. Avoid vague marketing language—use concrete specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 3: Customer Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 3: Customer Validation — Named beta customer; Specific use case; Measurable outcome; Quote from customer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete evidence from real users: name the customer (if allowed), describe the scenario, include metrics or measurable outcomes, and add a customer quote to lend credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 4: Quote from Founder/CTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 4: Quote from Founder/CTO — Substantive on technical approach; Specific on customer impact; Honest about what's still unsolved
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a meaningful leadership quote that adds insight (technical approach or product impact) and shows authenticity by acknowledging remaining limitations or roadmap items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 5: Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 5: Availability — Pricing tiers; Access method (signup, waitlist, sales); Geographic availability; Roadmap for upcoming features
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear how and when customers can get the product, the pricing model, any geographic restrictions, and next milestones so customers and press know what's next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate content
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate — Company description; Stage/scale; Total customers/users; Mission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, factual company background: what you do, company stage, scale metrics (users/customers), and mission statement. Keep it short and consistent across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia Requirements — Product screenshots; Demo video (under 90 seconds); Founder/team photos; Customer use case visualizations; Comparison charts where relevant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply a comprehensive media kit so journalists can quickly use assets: short demo video (<=90s), high-res screenshots, photos of founders/team, visuals that show customer workflows or outcomes, and comparative charts when helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution strategy options
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution Strategy — Embargoed exclusive to top trade outlet; Coordinated release across tech press; Wire syndication for SEO; Founder LinkedIn launch; Twitter/X founder thread; Hacker News submission (if relevant); Demo day at industry conference
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan distribution that fits the product and audience: consider an embargoed exclusive to a top outlet to build momentum, coordinate with tech press, use wire services for SEO, and amplify via founders' social channels and community platforms when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric for Product Launches (summary checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality Rubric for Product Launches — Genuinely new capability; Customer-validated; Demoable immediately; Specific use case included; Multimedia comprehensive; Founder available for demos; Pricing/availability clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as a final gate before issuing a press release: confirm the launch meets novelty, validation, demonstrability, specificity, media assets completeness, founder/demo availability, and clarity on pricing/availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder availability for demos
rubrics_metrics.description: Founder available for demos
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure a founder (or senior technical exec) is available for demos and interviews to support press coverage, answer technical questions, and provide credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing and availability must be clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Pricing/availability clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State pricing tiers, trial/beta conditions, how to access the product (signup/waitlist/sales), and geographic availability so customers and press aren't left with basic unanswered questions.
